subject: Creativity
title: Edward de Bono and Lateral Thinking
description: A quick, practical guide to Edward de Bono and Lateral Thinking.

hook.text: A truck got stuck under a bridge. Engineers debated raising the bridge. A child said: 'Let the air out of the tires.'

buildup.text: Edward de Bono coined 'lateral thinking' in 1967 — approaching problems indirectly instead of head-on.

discovery.text: Vertical thinking digs deeper in the same hole. Lateral thinking digs a new hole in a different place entirely.

twist.text: Lateral thinking isn't random. De Bono created specific techniques — provocations, reversals, analogies — to trigger it.

climax.text: Companies like IBM, Boeing, and Siemens trained thousands of employees in de Bono's lateral thinking methods.

punchline.text: When the obvious answer fails, try the absurd one. It might not be absurd.

quiz.question: What is lateral thinking?
options: Approaching problems indirectly instead of head-on

details.summary: Edward de Bono coined the term lateral thinking to describe approaching problems from unexpected angles rather than following logical steps. His techniques deliberately disrupt habitual thought patterns to produce novel solutions unavailable through linear reasoning.
details.whyItMatters: Lateral thinking provides practical tools for breaking out of mental ruts. De Bono's methods are used by corporations, governments, and educators worldwide to solve problems that resist conventional approaches.
takeaways: Lateral thinking approaches problems from non-obvious angles
De Bono created multiple practical techniques for lateral thinking
It complements rather than replaces logical vertical thinking

faq.question: How is lateral thinking different from brainstorming?
faq.answer: Brainstorming generates many ideas within existing mental frameworks. Lateral thinking deliberately breaks those frameworks by using provocations, reversals, and random entry points to force the mind into entirely new territory.

faq.question: Can lateral thinking be taught?
faq.answer: Yes. De Bono developed specific, learnable techniques including provocation, random word stimulation, and concept extraction. These are structured exercises that anyone can practice to develop lateral thinking skills.
